sourcedFrom: BANISH 22 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED (NOT PRINTED)
cleanIntro: A 5-3/8 inch, 1 inch diameter, 4.1 oz titanium rimfire can on a 1/2x28 direct thread, holding eight Link Together baffles. It comes apart from BOTH ends — a muzzle cap at the front and a breach cap at the counter-bore end — which is unlike every other Banish in this set. The whole design exists to fight lead: Banish requires cleaning every 100 to 200 rounds, and says outright that letting it go can make the can impossible to disassemble at all.

steps.title: Clear the host — magazine out, action locked open, safety on
steps.action: Remove the magazine, retract the bolt or slide and lock it open, then inspect the chamber visually AND physically to confirm the firearm is empty. Then engage the safety. Banish spells this sequence out for the Banish 22 rather than deferring to the host manual, and the safety step at the end is unusual — most of its books stop at the chamber check.
steps.prose: The wording covers a rifle or a pistol because this can goes on both. Whichever you have, the action is locked open before a finger goes near the chamber.
steps.quote: Remove the magazine from the firearm, retract the bolt or slide and lock it open.
steps.cite: BANISH 22 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — INSTALLATION OF SUPPRESSOR, p.4
steps.warn: Visually and physically inspect the chamber to ensure the firearm is empty and unloaded. Engage the safety.

steps.title: Banish 22 ceiling — .22 caliber and smaller, rimfire
steps.action: Check the host chambering. Banish designed this can for rimfire rifles and pistols of .22 caliber and smaller, and names .22 Hornet explicitly as included. The SPECS block reads CALIBER 22 and CALIBER RANGE .22 and Smaller, full auto rated.
steps.prose: Eight STifle baffles with Link Together Connection sit inside it, and Banish's stated reason for that design is to stop lead debris and carbon from fusing the baffles to each other or to the tube.
steps.quote: The BANISH 22 was designed for rimfire rifles and pistols, .22 caliber and smaller (including .22 Hornet).
steps.cite: BANISH 22 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — SPECS, p.3
steps.warn: .22 and smaller. This is a rimfire can.

steps.title: ⛔ Clean every 100-200 rounds or the can seizes shut
steps.action: Treat this as a hard requirement rather than a schedule. Unjacketed .22 bullets deposit lead as well as carbon, and Banish states plainly that cleaning is REQUIRED every 100 to 200 rounds to avoid having the baffles fuse together. Miss it far enough and the can becomes a solid object.
steps.prose: Every other Banish in this set has a maintenance interval. This one has a point of no return, and the manual describes it in the next sentence.
steps.quote: Cleaning is required every 100 - 200 rounds to avoid having the baffles fuse together.
steps.cite: BANISH 22 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — SPECS, p.3
steps.warn: 100-200 rounds. This is the shortest interval in the Banish line.

steps.title: What neglect actually does to this can
steps.action: Understand the failure mode before it happens. Banish describes it exactly: lead and carbon get AROUND the baffles and build on the inside of the tube, and that buildup then physically blocks the baffles from sliding out past it. At that point the can is no longer user-serviceable no matter what the specs say.
steps.prose: That is why the deep clean starts with penetrating oil and a soak rather than with a tool. The oil is what stops the buildup from becoming permanent.
steps.caution: A seized rimfire can is a warranty conversation, not a cleaning job.
steps.quote: If the lead and carbon get around the baffles (building up on the inside of the tube), it can prevent disassembly altogether. This will result in the baffles not being able to slide out past the buildup.
steps.cite: BANISH 22 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — SPECS, p.3

steps.title: Check the seat before firing and before stripping
steps.action: Confirm the threads on the barrel and the suppressor are clean and undamaged and that the can seats firmly against the shoulder. Take care not to cross-thread: on a 1 inch diameter can with fine 1/2x28 threads, cross-threading damages both the can and the barrel and misaligns the bore.
steps.prose: Banish names the consequence directly — a potential baffle strike that damages both the firearm and the suppressor.
steps.quote: Ensure the threads on the barrel and suppressor are clean and undamaged, screw the suppressor onto the barrel threads until the suppressor firmly seats against shoulder.
steps.cite: BANISH 22 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — INSTALLATION OF SUPPRESSOR, p.4
steps.warn: If there is any gap DO NOT fire the host with the silencer attached.

steps.title: Let it cool, or use a heat resistant glove
steps.action: After firing the can is very hot. Banish tells you to wait for it to cool or use a HEAT RESISTANT GLOVE to retighten and protect from burns — note this book specifies a glove rather than the suppressor cover its centrefire books offer.
steps.prose: 4.1 oz of titanium at 1 inch diameter has almost no thermal mass. It heats quickly on a full-auto rated .22 and it cools quickly too, so a short wait genuinely works.
steps.quote: Please note the suppressor will be very hot during and after firing. Wait until the suppressor cools or use a heat resistant glove to retighten and protect from burns.
steps.cite: BANISH 22 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — INSTALLATION OF SUPPRESSOR, p.4

steps.title: Unthread the Banish 22 off the muzzle
steps.action: With the host cleared and the safety on, turn the can counter-clockwise off the 1/2x28 threads. It goes on hand tight only, so it should come off by hand. Banish warns that thread mounted suppressors loosen or unscrew during firing, so the attachment has to be checked frequently rather than assumed.
steps.prose: On a semi-auto .22 the can can also walk tighter under a long string. Neither direction is safe to ignore.
steps.quote: Since thread mounted suppressors can loosen or unscrew during firing, it is extremely important that the operator frequently checks that the silencer remains securely threaded to the barrel.
steps.cite: BANISH 22 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — INSTALLATION OF SUPPRESSOR, p.4

steps.title: Protect the muzzle threads and never fire an obstructed can
steps.action: With the can off, fit a thread protector or muzzle device to the bare threads for storage and transport, and sight through the can before it goes back on. Banish's obstruction rule is absolute — mud, dirt or anything else in the bore and the host must not be fired.
steps.prose: On a rimfire can the most likely obstruction is your own oil: the deep clean ends with a film of oil on the baffles, and a heavy hand there leaves standing liquid.
steps.quote: Once the silencer is removed from the host firearm, BANISH recommends using a thread protector or other muzzle device to protect the muzzle threads and crown during storage or transport.
steps.cite: BANISH 22 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — WARNING, p.2
steps.warn: Silencers must be free of obstructions such as mud, dirt, etc.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: The Banish 22 is off the host and the threads are covered — that is the routine strip. The two-cap teardown is the Deep Clean, and on this can it is not optional maintenance: Banish's own interval is 100 to 200 rounds because the alternative is a can that will not come apart.
steps.prose: Banish also says most .22 suppressors can be disassembled for cleaning, which is the whole reason this one has caps at both ends.
steps.quote: It is recommended that the suppressor be cleaned regularly. To disassemble make sure the firearm is unloaded and remove from host firearm.
steps.cite: BANISH 22 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — CLEANING, p.5

deepSteps.title: Muzzle cap off with the tool key, then the breach cap
deepSteps.action: With the can off the host, use the supplied tool key to remove the MUZZLE cap from the front, then take off the BREACH cap at the other end. This can is the only Banish in the set that opens from both ends, and both caps come off before the baffles can move.
deepSteps.prose: Keep the two caps identifiable as they come off. They are not interchangeable and putting the breach cap on the wrong end is the specific error the manual warns about later.
deepSteps.caution: Muzzle cap and breach cap are different parts for different ends.
deepSteps.quote: Using the provided tool key, remove the muzzle cap of the suppressor. Remove the breach cap.
deepSteps.cite: BANISH 22 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — CLEANING, p.5

deepSteps.title: Penetrating oil, 1 to 2 hours — not a solvent, not 24 hours
deepSteps.action: Soak the inside of the tube and the baffles with a PENETRATING OIL and leave it 1 to 2 hours. Note both differences from the centrefire Banish books: penetrating oil rather than a carbon solvent, and one to two hours rather than twenty-four. This is lead you are lifting, not carbon you are dissolving.
deepSteps.prose: Penetrating oil creeps between the baffle and the tube wall, which is exactly where the fusing happens on a rimfire can.
deepSteps.quote: Soak the inside of the tube and baffles with a penetrating oil and let sit for 1 - 2 hours.
deepSteps.cite: BANISH 22 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — CLEANING, p.5
deepSteps.warn: Penetrating oil, 1-2 hours. Do not carry the 24 hour solvent soak across from a centrefire Banish book.

deepSteps.title: Push the baffles out only if they need it
deepSteps.action: After the soak, the eight Link Together baffles should come out of the tube. Where fouling has been heavy, Banish's optional Baffle Remove Tool can be used to push them — and it adds a caution: care must be taken to avoid damage to the baffles. If the stack will not move, the answer is more soak time, not more force.
deepSteps.prose: This is the point where a neglected can announces itself. Baffles that will not slide past the buildup are the failure the manual described on page 3.
deepSteps.caution: Force is the wrong answer. Soak longer.
deepSteps.quote: If excessive fouling has occurred, our Baffle Remove Tool (sold separately) can be used to push the baffles out. Care must be taken to avoid damage to the baffles.
deepSteps.cite: BANISH 22 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — CLEANING, p.5

deepSteps.title: Nylon brush, then a light film of oil
deepSteps.action: Scrub the baffles and the tube with a NYLON brush to take the carbon off — nylon, not brass, on this can. Once every part is clean AND dry, put a light film of oil on the baffles specifically to help them go back in.
deepSteps.prose: That oil film is an assembly aid, not corrosion protection. Light is the operative word: heavy oil in a rimfire can burns to varnish on the next string.
deepSteps.quote: Scrub the baffles and tube with a nylon brush to remove carbon deposits. Once all parts are clean and dry, add a light film of oil on the baffles, to aid in assembly
deepSteps.cite: BANISH 22 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — CLEANING, p.5

deepSteps.title: Grease the internal threads, then find the counter-bore end
deepSteps.action: Apply a small amount of grease or anti-seize to the threads inside the tube. Then find the counter bore — it is the SHORT end — and install the breach cap there hand tight. Banish gives you a positive test: if the breach cap fails to shoulder against the tube, it is on the wrong end.
deepSteps.prose: That test is the whole reason this step is separate. A cap that will not shoulder is telling you which way round the tube is, and no amount of turning will fix a wrong end.
deepSteps.quote: Inside the tube, locate the end with the counter bore (short end) and install the breach cap hand tight. If the breach cap fails to shoulder against the tube it is on the wrong end.
deepSteps.cite: BANISH 22 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — ASSEMBLY, p.5
deepSteps.warn: A breach cap that will not shoulder is on the wrong end. Stop and turn the tube around.

deepSteps.title: Baffles back in — shortest one LAST, etched lines aligned
deepSteps.action: Reinstall the eight baffles into the tube with the SHORTEST baffle going in last. Each baffle carries a faint etched line on its side to help you line them up, so rotate each one so those lines agree as the stack builds.
deepSteps.prose: The etched lines are easy to miss under fresh oil. Find them on a clean baffle in good light before you start feeding them in.
deepSteps.caution: Shortest baffle last. It is the only one that is not interchangeable.
deepSteps.quote: Reinstall the baffles into the tube placing the shortest baffle last. Each baffle has a faint line etched on the side to aid in alignment.
deepSteps.cite: BANISH 22 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — ASSEMBLY, p.5

deepSteps.title: Muzzle cap back on — hand tight with the tool key
deepSteps.action: Refit the muzzle cap using the provided key tool, HAND TIGHT. There is no torque figure in this book and no inch-pound spec anywhere in it — unlike the centrefire Banish cans, which finish at 110-120 or 40 in-lbs. Hand tight is the specification for this can.
deepSteps.prose: On a 1 inch titanium tube with fine cap threads, reaching for a torque figure borrowed from a bigger can is how the cap threads get stripped.
deepSteps.quote: Reinstall the muzzle cap hand tight with the provided key tool.
deepSteps.cite: BANISH 22 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — ASSEMBLY, p.5
deepSteps.warn: Hand tight. No torque figure is published for this can.

cleaning.name: BAFFLES AND TUBE
tasks: Soak the tube interior and baffles with penetrating oil for 1 to 2 hours
Use the Baffle Remove Tool only if fouling is heavy, and take care not to damage the baffles
Scrub the baffles and the tube with a NYLON brush
Add a light film of oil to the baffles once everything is clean and dry, to aid assembly

cleaning.name: CAPS AND THREADS
tasks: Remove the muzzle cap with the provided tool key, then the breach cap
Grease or anti-seize the threads inside the tube before reassembly
Fit the breach cap at the counter-bore (short) end — it must shoulder against the tube
Refit the muzzle cap hand tight with the tool key; no torque figure applies

cleaning.name: MUZZLE INTERFACE
tasks: Clean the 1/2x28 barrel threads while the can is off
Check the can's threads are undamaged before it goes back on
Fit a thread protector for storage and transport

cleaning.name: SCHEDULE
tasks: Clean every 100 to 200 rounds — required, not recommended, to stop the baffles fusing
Check the can is still securely threaded to the barrel frequently while shooting
Never fire the host with an obstructed can

reassembly: Apply a small amount of grease or anti-seize to the threads inside the tube.
Find the counter-bore (short) end and install the breach cap there hand tight; if it will not shoulder against the tube, it is on the wrong end.
Reinstall the eight baffles with their faint etched alignment lines lined up, placing the shortest baffle last.
Refit the muzzle cap hand tight with the provided key tool.
Thread the can back onto the 1/2x28 muzzle hand tight, seating firmly against the shoulder without cross-threading.
fncheck: With both caps hand tight, sight through the Banish 22 and confirm the eight baffle bores line up as one clear channel — the etched alignment lines are what should have got you there. Check the breach cap has shouldered fully against the tube; if it has not, it is on the wrong end and the can is not assembled. Confirm no standing oil is left inside, then fit it to the muzzle hand tight and check it seats against the shoulder with no gap.
